newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber close higher, but off early limit gain.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber close higher, but off early limit gain.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed higher in nearby months and lower in deferreds, with strong cash prices supporting January and March contract, traders said.
The strong cash markets, plus doubts about future lumber demand, encouraged active bull-spreading, which weighed on the deferred months, they said.
On Wednesday, Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $394.00 per tbf, but traders said prices have since traded near $405.

However, analysts said futures may be near a peak and could trend lower soon. Typical holiday slowdowns at mills and by home builders should lead to a down trend in lumber futures later this month, they said.
Lumber closed up $6.10 to down $2.50 with January up the most at $415.40 per tbf.
